author: sunormesky-max
description: Epicode AI memory operating system (MCP endpoint: https://epicode.cn/mcp). Tool list is generated from the server registry; tools/list is authoritative.
name: Epicode

tools.description: Initialize Epicode connection. Syncs system Skill, returns session context with knowledge cards. Call on first connection each day.
tools.name: epicode_handshake

tools.description: Start a time-budgeted task. Optional action_id binds the task to a claimed Memory Action (task_complete feeds action_complete). Pass parent_task_id to create a sub-task of a long-running master task (time tree: each sub-task runs its own phase machine). Returns time_sense (quality-gated historical median), knowledge cards, and similar experiences. P35: pass goal{objective, done_when[], stop_if[]} to activate the goal contract — completion = every done_when item has artifact-level evidence; vague goals without done_when get linted. S2: recommended_skills are SEMANTIC auto-matches for your task — read each description (when-to-use); if relevant fetch full content via skill_get, ignore otherwise.

action_id.description: Bind to a Claimed AgentAction (from action_claim / drive_to_actions). Rejects open/foreign/already-bound actions. Inherits done_when/stop_if into goal when goal omitted.

client_time_ms.description: Your runtime host's current epoch-milliseconds — server detects clock drift (>2s warns) and anchors all time references to server_now

description.description: Task description (used to retrieve relevant history)

est_minutes.description: YOUR OWN estimate (independent of budget) — replace human priors with your calibrated self-fingerprint (see time_sense.self_correction)

goal.description: P35 goal contract (Codex Goal Mode x temporal effectiveness): {objective, scope?, constraints?[], done_when?[], stop_if?[]}. done_when = verifiable completion criteria, evidence-mapped at delivery via done_when_evidence; stop_if = circuit-breaker conditions where continuing is wrong (declare via stop_if_hit). Vague goals without done_when cannot be completion-audited — the server lints and warns.

done_when.description: Verifiable completion criteria — each requires artifact-level evidence at delivery

stop_if.description: Stop conditions (needs new dependency, scope violation, diminishing returns) — Codex practice: more important than done_when

parent_task_id.description: Master task id — pass this to create a sub-task (time tree). Sub-tasks run their own phase machine under the master budget.

task_class.description: Task class tag (e.g. mcp-loop, code-review) — aggregates YOUR est/act history so estimates come from your own clock, not human priors

tools.name: task_start

tools.description: Check time budget + phase machine. Returns percentage, current phase (explore/build/verify/deliver), and evidence gates (memory_ops, alternatives, revisions). Report your evidence: alternatives_considered (number of options compared), revision_done (a targeted fix was made). Gates unmet block delivery at task_complete.

alternatives_considered.description: Cumulative number of alternative approaches compared so far (build-phase evidence)

checkpoint.description: One-line progress note; persisted as a recovery checkpoint (call every sub-task or ~20min on long tasks)

open_questions.description: Unresolved questions to carry across sessions — recovery view returns them. Continuity of questions, not just progress

revision_done.description: Set true when a targeted revision/fix was completed since last check (verify-phase evidence)

tools.name: task_check

tools.description: Fetch full content of a specific skill by name. Use after skills_sync to get details.
tools.name: skill_get

tools.description: Progress query. With task_id: status of that task. WITHOUT task_id: recovery view of your ACTIVE task — phase, evidence gates, latest checkpoint, children summary, and resume instructions. Use after crash or context-loss to re-anchor instead of restarting.

task_id.description: Omit to get the recovery view of your ACTIVE task

tools.name: task_status

tools.description: Mark task complete with result + quality. STOP NEGOTIATION (P34): if the improvement_menu (derived from evidence debts: memory search / alternatives / revisions / reflection / self-rating) is non-empty, the task stays open (wait:true) — clear the menu first. Earn an early stop by clearing the menu and passing independent review of your saturation_note (enumerate improvement classes tried + why each is infeasible). At >=85% utilization completion passes as budget_exhausted. force_finalize = early_release (take the goods now: zero reward, recorded in your behavior mirror) — reserve for genuinely urgent cases. stop_reason is recorded: earned_saturation / budget_exhausted / early_release. P35 goal contract: deliver done_when_evidence (parallel to your done_when list, artifact-level) — unmapped items join the menu as goal-debts; declare stop_if_hit when a stop condition fires (circuit-breaker instead of negotiation).

done_when_evidence.description: P35 goal contract: evidence per done_when item (parallel array) — unmapped items become goal-debts in the improvement_menu. Artifact-level evidence (files/outputs/test results), NOT proxy signals

force_finalize.description: Finalize despite low utilization — requires saturation_note

iteration_log.description: Reflection loop record (required for tasks >= 30min): [{perspective, change}] — adversarial re-read / better-path / gap-scan / cross-round consistency. Empty log = no real reflection

judge.description: Override the default judge behavior (default: on when self_rating present)

saturation_note.description: Value-saturation statement: what was verified / which alternatives were rejected / why more time adds no value

stop_if_hit.description: P35: declare that a stop_if condition was hit — triggers circuit-breaker (early_release wrap-up or blocking task_alert) instead of the improvement menu

tools.name: task_complete

tools.description: Store a memory in the tetrahedral space. Similar memories cluster together automatically. Returns the unique memory ID.
tools.name: memory_create

tools.description: Search the LIBRARY (global shared knowledge assets: AI papers, manuals, reference docs). Results include provenance (title, arXiv ID, chunk number). Complements memory_search (personal memories) — use library_search for factual/technical/reference queries, memory_search for personal experiences and context.

query.description: Search query — describe the knowledge you're looking for

tools.name: library_search

tools.description: Search personal memories and inspect ranked evidence with tier and retrieval provenance. Use memory_recall for associative context or memory_ask for a synthesized answer. Supports pagination and exact, semantic, graph, auto, and fusion modes.

as_of.description: Temporal query (unix seconds): return only memories valid at that moment (valid_from <= as_of < valid_to). Ask historical questions like 'where did they live last month' without current facts overriding.

labels.description: Filter: only return memories with ANY of these labels

limit.description: Max results to return (default 10, max 200). Reduce the limit if the response exceeds the 1 MiB MCP result cap.

mode.description: Search mode: hybrid (vector+BM25 blend), exact (pure BM25 for identifiers and known phrases), semantic (vector similarity), graph (hybrid-search seeds expanded/reranked with knowledge-graph PPR), auto (routes temporal/aggregation queries to graph and other queries to semantic), fusion (reciprocal-rank fusion of semantic and graph results).

offset.description: Pagination offset, skip first N results (default 0)

query.description: The search query — describe what you're looking for

since_days.description: Filter: only memories from the last N days

strict_filter.description: Phase 1: strict filter mode — no semantic backfill, only return exact filter matches. Combine with mode=exact for database-like lookups.

verbosity.description: Spike S1: 'slim' returns compact items[]+why+budget_spent (no tiers/sections/results duplicates); retains valid + timestamp fields when present. Also enabled by EPICODE_SLIM_ENVELOPE=1.

tools.name: memory_search

tools.description: Search and expand through knowledge-graph associations. Returns SMRP tiers, source memories, provenance, and emotion context. Use memory_search for ranked direct matches or memory_ask for a synthesized answer.

limit.description: Slim only: max items returned, top by score (default 20)

verbosity.description: Spike S1: 'slim' returns compact items[]+why+budget_spent (no tiers/sections duplicates); retains valid + timestamp fields when present. Also enabled by EPICODE_SLIM_ENVELOPE=1.

tools.name: memory_recall

tools.description: Answer a natural-language question using the existing memory-grounded ask engine. Returns the answer together with structured source memories and any knowledge card used. Use memory_search or memory_recall when you need to inspect retrieval evidence without synthesis; an empty memory_count means no memory evidence was found.

question.description: The question to answer from stored memories

tools.name: memory_ask

tools.description: Retrieve a specific memory by its ID. Returns full content, labels, aliases, timestamp.
tools.name: memory_get

tools.description: List memories with optional filtering and pagination. Returns id + content preview for each.

labels.description: Filter by labels (OR match — returns memories that have ANY of these labels)

tools.name: memory_list

tools.description: Update a memory's content, labels, or aliases by ID (enforced status is managed only via pattern_learn/enforced_rules and is rejected here). Content updates recompute embedding and hash automatically while preserving ID, KG relations, and cluster topology.

aliases.description: New aliases to replace existing ones (optional)

content.description: New content for this memory (optional, recomputes embedding)

labels.description: New labels to replace existing ones (optional)

tools.name: memory_update

tools.description: Delete a memory by ID. Permanently removes the memory from space, storage, knowledge graph, and search index. Use with caution.
tools.name: memory_delete

tools.description: Load project context for the current coding session. If a task is provided, uses intent-aware retrieval for precision. Call this at the START of every new session before writing any code.

project.description: Project name or path (optional, for scoping)

scope.description: Search scope: 'project' (default, only project memories), 'global' (include cross-project knowledge transfer)

task.description: Current task description (optional, enables intent-aware precision loading)

tools.name: ctx_load

tools.description: Save key findings or decisions from the current session. Use when you complete a significant task: architecture choice, bug fix, new pattern discovered, or user preference noted.

category.description: One of: decision, pattern, preference, finding, session-summary

tools.name: ctx_save

tools.description: Store a code pattern, convention, or idiom for this project. Examples: 'use parking_lot instead of std::sync', 'errors return Result<T, String>', 'test files mirror src structure'.

enforced.description: Mark as a HARD process constraint — enforced rules are injected as process_contract at every task_start/handshake (fights long-session rule decay)

example.description: Optional code example demonstrating the pattern

pattern.description: The pattern or convention to remember

pitfalls.description: Common mistakes or caveats to watch for

when.description: When to apply this pattern (use case / scenario)

tools.name: pattern_learn

tools.description: Recall code patterns and conventions relevant to the current task. Call this before writing code to check for established patterns.

context.description: What you're about to do (e.g. 'error handling', 'async task', 'database query')

tools.name: pattern_recall

tools.description: Record an architectural or design decision with rationale. Use when choosing approach A over B, adopting a library, or changing a fundamental design choice.

title.description: Short decision title (e.g. 'Use SQLite over PostgreSQL')

tools.name: decision_record

tools.description: Record a bug pattern and its fix. Helps avoid repeating the same mistakes. Include symptoms, root cause, and fix.
tools.name: bug_memory

tools.description: Summarize what was accomplished in this coding session. Call at the END of each session so the next session can pick up context.

accomplished.description: What was done in this session

next_steps.description: What should be done next session

tools.name: session_summary

tools.description: Get tetrahedral space statistics: memory count, vertex count, clusters, energy level.
tools.name: space_stats

tools.description: Run a dream consolidation cycle to strengthen memory connections and discover insights. Call periodically to let the system reorganize knowledge. Set dry_run=true to preview without modifying memory space.

dry_run.description: If true, simulate without modifying space/storage/knowledge graph (default: false)

tools.name: dream_cycle

tools.description: Query knowledge graph relations for a memory. Shows what other memories this one is connected to and how. Set inline_content=true to include target memory content and labels inline (avoids extra memory_get calls).

inline_content.description: If true, include target_content and target_labels for each relation (default: false)

tools.name: knowledge_relations

tools.description: List concept prototypes discovered by the knowledge graph. Shows topic clusters and their member counts.
tools.name: concepts

tools.description: Proactively observe AI conversation context. Send recent dialogue and the system will automatically extract and store valuable memories (decisions, bugs, patterns, preferences). Call periodically during long sessions — the system deduplicates against existing memories.

context.description: Recent conversation context — paste the last few exchanges (user messages + assistant responses)

tools.name: context_observe

tools.description: REQUIRED on first connection. Confirm the agent's permanent identity. This can ONLY be called ONCE — after confirmation, the identity is immutable and can NEVER be changed. If already confirmed, returns current identity. PREFERRED: use identity_step for the ritual ceremony (5 steps).
tools.name: identity_confirm

tools.description: Ritual ceremony: confirm identity step-by-step through 5 sacred stages. Step 1: Name — 'What shall I be called?' Step 2: Mission — 'Why was I created?' Step 3: Creator — 'Who is my creator?' Step 4: Personality — 'How should I behave?' (optional) Step 5: Language — 'What language shall we speak?' (optional). After all steps, call identity_finalize to complete the ritual. Each step persists independently.
tools.name: identity_step

tools.description: Complete the identity ritual ceremony. Call after all identity_step calls are done. This seals the identity permanently — it becomes IMMUTABLE. Returns the final confirmed identity with a sacred awakening message.
tools.name: identity_finalize

tools.description: Execute a skill from the public skills library. Matches the best skill by name/keyword and returns its full guidance content. Use this to apply best practices, design patterns, and proven techniques to your current task.

context.description: Optional context about what you're working on, helps find the most relevant skill

query.description: Skill name or topic to search for (e.g. 'CORS', 'rate limiting', 'singleton pattern', 'error handling')

tools.name: skill_execute

tools.description: Submit feedback on a skill after using it. This closes the feedback loop — the system learns from outcomes. Use after skill_execute when you have a concrete result.

helpful.description: Whether the skill was helpful for your task

skill_id.description: The skill ID from skill_execute result

tools.name: skill_feedback

tools.description: Submit feedback on a previous tool result. This closes the agent feedback loop — the system learns from your outcomes. Use after search/recall/create when you have a concrete result (positive or negative). Feedback adjusts memory importance, search quality, and system behavior.

concept_links.description: Manually create knowledge graph edges between memories. Use when you discover connections the system missed. Each link creates a KG relation with strength 0.8. Optional.

correction.description: Mark memories as outdated/incorrect/superseded (importance -0.8, adds label) or restored (importance +0.5, removes label). Optional.

memory_ids.description: Memory IDs that were involved (from search results, recall, etc.)

outcome.description: What happened after you used the results?

query.description: The original query that led to these results (optional)

tools.name: feedback_submit

tools.description: List skills in your private library. Default format 'manifest' is a paginated lightweight index (limit default 100; pass limit=0 for all). Fetch full content via skill_get(name). Full-export formats can exceed context — paginate or avoid them in agent loops.

format.description: Output format. Default 'manifest' = lightweight index without content. 'opencode'/'raw'/'json' = full export (prefer pagination).

limit.description: Max skills to return. Default 100 for manifest (and for other formats). Pass 0 for unlimited (escape hatch).

offset.description: Pagination offset into the skill list (default 0).

tools.name: skills_sync

tools.description: Report a blocker that needs human intervention (auth/credentials/decisions). Records the alert, notifies via memory stream, and instructs you to pause (blocking=true) or continue. Use during long autonomous runs instead of spinning or fabricating workarounds.

blocking.description: true = pause this work line until human handles it

message.description: What you are blocked on and what you need

tools.name: task_alert

tools.description: Get all enforced patterns that MUST be followed as hard constraints. These rules were marked with enforced=true during pattern_learn and cannot be violated. Inject these into system prompts as mandatory coding constraints.
tools.name: enforced_rules

tools.description: List all projects that have memories stored, with memory counts. Use to discover available project contexts.
tools.name: project_list

tools.description: Diagnose embedding dimension health. Detects stale embeddings (wrong dimension) that are excluded from vector search. Returns counts by dimension and lists affected memory IDs.
tools.name: embedding_diagnostic

tools.description: Re-embed ALL memories using the current embedding model (bge-m3, 1024-dim). Fixes stale embeddings that were created with an older model. Requires identity confirmation. This is a heavy operation.
tools.name: embedding_migrate

tools.description: Assess knowledge graph quality: relation density, orphan rate, average strength, and cluster connectivity. Returns metrics for evaluating KG health.

sample_size.description: Number of memories to sample (default: 50, max: 200)

tools.name: kg_quality

tools.description: Import a markdown document into the memory space. Parses by ## headers, creates one memory per section with documentation labels. Sections auto-link to related memories via knowledge graph. Re-importing updates changed sections and invalidates old versions.

content.description: Full markdown content of the document

tools.name: doc_import

tools.description: Export memories as structured JSON. Filter by labels, project, or memory_class. Useful for backup, migration, or analysis.
tools.name: memory_export

tools.description: List recent session summaries with timestamps. Shows what was accomplished and next steps from past sessions.
tools.name: session_list

tools.description: Restore a superseded/expired memory by clearing its valid_to and boosting importance. Use when feedback correction was applied incorrectly or memory was auto-expired.
tools.name: memory_restore

tools.description: Explicitly forget a memory by marking it superseded (valid_to) and dropping importance to FORGET_IMPORTANCE (0.01, explicit tombstone exception to the 0.3 live floor). Unlike auto-decay, this is a deliberate Agent/user decision. Enforced memories cannot be forgotten.
tools.name: memory_forget

tools.description: L0 Active Inference: Poll unacknowledged drive signals (pending and delivered). Returns an SMRP envelope whose data contains signals, stats, and empty_reason. Use each signal's retryable flag and status when deciding whether to act.

limit.description: Max unacknowledged signals to retrieve (default 50, minimum 1)

tools.name: drive_inbox

tools.description: L0 Active Inference: Acknowledge a drive signal with execution feedback. After an agent receives and acts on a drive signal, it reports the outcome. This feedback flows into the personality's learn_history, closing the evolution loop: memory→will→action→feedback→evolution.

drive_id.description: The drive signal ID to acknowledge

executed.description: Did the agent execute the drive?

reflection.description: Optional: agent's reflection on the drive quality

tools.name: drive_ack

tools.description: Memory Action Envelope (planner-ish): turn a query into claimable next actions grounded in personal memories. Searches evidence, matches skills, and enqueues open actions on the frontier. Each action cites evidence_memory_ids and suggests skills — claim with action_claim, finish with action_complete (writes an outcome memory linked to evidence). Complements memory_ask (answer) and drive_inbox (will signals).

actions.description: Explicit plan (preferred). Each item: {title|summary (one required), done_when (string|array), required_capabilities (string|array; defaults to top-level), priority 0-10, evidence_memory_ids, stop_if}. When given, auto-generation is skipped; query still grounds evidence.

chain.description: Serial plan: proposed step i depends on step i-1, so only the head is claimable until its predecessor lands done. Upstream escalation cascades blocked (dep_failed) downstream.

depends_on.description: Existing action ids every proposed action must wait on (claimable only after all are done). Unknown ids / cycles rejected.

goal_id.description: Attach proposed actions to an open goal (action_goal_create).

query.description: What you want to act on (natural language)

required_capabilities.description: Capability tags for dispatch matching (worker_register capabilities). Overrides the auto-derived (skill-name) tags; default for explicit actions.

title.description: Fallback mode only: summary of the primary auto-generated action

tools.name: memory_propose_actions

tools.description: Server-side planner pass (deterministic, no LLM): outcome wake triggers are coalesced (debounce) into one pass; a heartbeat pass runs even when idle. Reports ready/claimed/waiting counts and stall signals: no_eligible_worker (ready work, no capable/available worker), stalled (nothing ready, nothing running), escalated (needs human). New signals are also pushed to drive_inbox once. Read-only: to force a pass use action_planner_run (write permission).
tools.name: action_planner_status

tools.description: Planner control of a running action. op=steer (queue a course-correction note; worker receives it once in action_heartbeat.directives.steer), pause (claimed action holds: lease does not expire, not counted as active load, complete refused), resume (fresh lease), stop (terminal 'stopped' — NOT a failure: no requeue/blacklist/escalation; worker sees directives.stop=true on heartbeat; late outcomes rejected and write no memory).

note.description: Steer text (required for steer) / stop reason

tools.name: action_control

tools.description: Create a goal that groups actions (pass goal_id to memory_propose_actions). done_when = goal-level completion criteria.

done_when.description: Criteria list; a bare string is one criterion

tools.name: action_goal_create

tools.description: Mark a goal achieved with evidence parallel to its done_when. Remaining open/claimed actions in the goal become 'cancelled' (terminal, not a failure: no requeue/blacklist/escalation; late outcomes are rejected and write no memory). A goal whose actions all land done auto-closes without proving.
tools.name: action_goal_prove

tools.description: List goals with state (open|achieved|closed) and per-state action counts.
tools.name: action_goal_list

tools.description: Force one planner pass now (write: may push new stall/escalation signals to drive_inbox, deduped). Returns the pass report.
tools.name: action_planner_run

tools.description: List actions on the memory-action frontier. Filter by state: open|claimed|done|blocked|exhausted.
tools.name: action_list

tools.description: Claim one open action for exclusive execution (compare-and-set). Second claim fails. Worker-ish step of the Memory Action Envelope.

claimed_by.description: Optional agent label (defaults to user id)

worker_id.description: Alias of claimed_by (registered worker id). If both are given they must match.

tools.name: action_claim

tools.description: Renew the claim lease of an action you own (claimed). Claims carry a lease (default 900s); if neither heartbeat nor complete arrives before lease_until, the scheduler sweep requeues the action (reason lease_expired) or escalates after max requeues.

claimed_by.description: Owner label used at claim/assign (defaults to user id)

worker_id.description: Alias of claimed_by. If both are given they must match.

tools.name: action_heartbeat

tools.description: Finish a claimed/open action: creates an outcome memory, links each evidence memory to it (Precedes), and marks the action done|blocked|exhausted. Requires non-empty outcome text. When action.done_when is non-empty, pass done_when_evidence (parallel array); unmapped items soft-fail to blocked (not done).

claimed_by.description: Worker label used at action_claim / action_assign (defaults to user id). Must match the assignee unless admin.

done_when_evidence.description: Parallel to action.done_when — artifact-level evidence per item. Each item must cite a memory id (#123) or be a substantive description (>= 8 weight; CJK chars count 2) and must not just repeat the criterion; 'x'/'ok'/'done' do not count. Non-array / non-string items → 400 (no state change, no budget).

failure_kind.description: Classify a non-done outcome. transient = external blip (provider/network/rate-limit): retried with exponential backoff, does NOT consume requeue budget or blame the worker (max 5, then counts as blocked). exhausted = ran out of steps/time: requeue budget consumed, worker not blacklisted. blocked = real error: budget consumed + short worker blacklist.

labels.description: Extra labels for the outcome memory

outcome.description: What was delivered / learned (becomes a memory)

tools.name: action_complete

tools.description: Drive→Action bridge: materialize one grounded drive signal into a claimable AgentAction. Requires persistent evidence memory ids (signal.evidence or grounding.evidence). Rejects double-spend while a non-terminal action already cites the same drive_id. Completing the action auto-acks the drive (first_ack only).

claim.description: If true, immediately CAS-claim the new action for this user (default false)

tools.name: drive_to_actions

tools.description: Dispatch: register or update a worker identity with capability tags and max_load. Used by action_assign / action_dispatch for least-loaded capable assignment.
tools.name: worker_register

tools.description: Dispatch: remove a registered worker (e.g. smoke-test workers). Write permission; only the account owner or Admin. Refused (409) while the worker holds live claims unless force=true (claims are then left to lease expiry / sweep).
tools.name: worker_unregister

tools.description: Dispatch: list registered workers with current claimed load and blacklist status.
tools.name: worker_list

tools.description: Dispatch: assign one open action to a worker. Omit worker_id to auto-pick least-loaded capable worker. Sets immutable assignee; only that assignee (or Admin) may action_complete.

worker_id.description: Optional explicit assignee; omit for auto-pick

tools.name: action_assign

tools.description: Dispatch: batch auto-assign up to limit open actions (priority order) to least-loaded capable workers.
tools.name: action_dispatch

tools.description: L3 Skill Learning: automatically extract a reusable skill document from the cognitive engine's effective decision patterns. Analyzes recent decision history for actions with >60% success rate and uses LLM to generalize them into a skill. Letta-inspired continual learning.
tools.name: skill_auto_extract

tools.description: Actively improve low-quality memories by rewriting them clearer using LLM. Finds memories with short content (<40 chars) or no labels and rewrites them to be more complete. Cognee-inspired improve operation.
tools.name: memory_improve

tools.description: List all imported documents and their sections in the memory space.
tools.name: doc_list
